subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should OpenClaw treat gateway operator scopes as an input to agent tool-policy resolution, and what public config/API shape and precedence should own it?
rationale: Current docs define operator scopes as trusted-domain control-plane guardrails, while this RFC would make them part of runtime tool authorization for multi-user deployments.

options.title: Decide scope model first
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose the trust boundary, config/API shape, and precedence before implementation.

options.title: Route to session envelopes
options.body: Make per-session runtime envelopes the canonical policy input and leave operator scopes as gateway method authorization only.

options.title: Fold into tenant RBAC
options.body: Defer this focused RFC into the broader tenant-RBAC design if operator scopes should only change inside a first-class tenant model.

recommendation.title: Decide scope model first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose the trust boundary, config/API shape, and precedence before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged scoped conversation capability profile and recent operator-scope/security docs that frame the decision.
